text:
yasmin: quick sync — thinking about how we flip the new eviction flag for prefix KV migration. want a rollout plan that avoids R/W flaps during handoffs.

devon: +1. main risk is a partial toggle where some nodes use new grace scoring and others don't, causing reads to see different residency assumptions.

trent: can we do a two-bit feature flag per shard: (1) admission-migration-enabled, (2) eviction-policy-v2? then sequence: enable admission, observe, then eviction.

emma: that seems safer. admission-first prevents new prefixes from being served into old slab layout. but we need a way to drain existing prefix ownerships without forcing massive demotions.

devon: propose a lightweight drain mode: when eviction-policy-v2=false but admission-migration-enabled=true, new prefixes get migrated to v2 slab, existing ones marked as "drainable" and moved lazily on demote/evict.

yasmin: nice. what metrics do we watch to catch divergence?

trent: track: prefix-residency-version by tenant, eviction-rate-v1 vs v2, read-latency-delta, and a per-shard "cross-version-read-retries" counter for any read-after-write mismatches.

emma: add a canary that toggles both flags on a single shard pair for 15m under low traffic, run synthetic rw tests: create prefix, write, read immediately from other node. also validate cursor resume across demote.

devon: sample flag config we'd push to rollout-service: ```json
{
  "target": "shard:42",
  "flags": {
    "admission_migration": true,
    "eviction_policy_v2": false
  },
  "duration": "15m"
}```

emma: rollback criteria: cross-version-read-retries > 5/min OR read-latency-delta > 50ms sustained for 5m OR customer errors increment > baseline by 0.1%.

yasmin: good. ops questions: do we need a compatibility shim in the handoff protocol so receiver can accept older pointer metadata?

devon: yes — introduce a tiny compatibility layer: when receiver sees prefix.metadata.version < local_min_version, it will accept and mark the prefix as "compat-stub" that forces an eager verify on first read (no KV prefetch). reduces correctness risk at expense of first-read latency.

trent: can we detect that from the sequencer to avoid roundtrip cost? i.e., sequencer annotates handoff with source_version to allow faster short-circuit. if not present, fall back to compat-stub.

emma: good optimization. make sure the sequencer annotation is idempotent and signed in the handoff token. otherwise race when retried looks like a mismatch.

yasmin: testing plan: 1) unit tests for compat-stub path, 2) integration chaos (drop handoff ACKs), 3) canary shard synthetic traffic, 4) gradual 10%->50%->100% with metrics gating.

devon: I'll draft the rollout playbook and a list of dashboards/alerts. leaving note to ops: when toggling eviction_policy_v2 cluster-wide, allow 30m quiesce for slow demotes.

infra-bot: deploy triggered: feature-flags/rollout/8501239876 started by devon — canary target shard:42 for 15m. :rocket:

emma: thanks — ping me when canary completes, i'll run the rw probe script.

yasmin: perfect. also add a post-rollout audit job to scan for tenants with mixed residency versions and emit ticket if >100 prefixes affected.

devon: noted. I'll post the playbook link after I write it. :+1:
